sentences.text:
Mr. Bhaskar Sen, Sr. Adv.
Mr. Kaushik Gupta ..learned advocates for the petitioner.
Mr. Anindya Sundar Chatterjee Mr. Gautam Dinda .. learned advocates for the opposite party no.1.

The grievance of the petitioner is against a proceeding arising out of case no.1D of 2002 under Section 16(1)(a)(i) read with Section 7 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 pending before the learned Metropolitan and Municipal Magistrate, 4th Court, Kolkata wherein process was issued against the petitioner along with two others vide order dated January 25, 2002 on the basis of a petition of complaint filed by the Food Inspector, Kolkata Municipal Corporation who is the opposite party no. 1 herein.

entities.text: Metropolitan and Municipal Magistrate, 4th Court, Kolkata
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Mr. Sen, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that a complaint against the director of the company is not maintainable unless a criminal act is specified against him.

It is argued that there is no allegation in the petition of complaint against this petitioner who is the Director of the company named M/s. Switz Food (P) Ltd. so the proceeding as regards this petitioner is liable to be quashed.

To fortify his submission learned advocate for the petitioner placed reliance upon the decision reported in 1983 Supreme Court Cases (Cri) 115 in the case of Municipal Corporation of Delhi -Versus- Ram Kishan Rohtagi And Others.

entities.text: Municipal Corporation of Delhi -Versus- Ram Kishan Rohtagi And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reference has also been made to a decision of Punjab and Haryana High Court in the case of Subhash Chand @ Subhash K. Aggarwal - Versus- State (Chandigarh Administration), Chandigarh, reported in 2011(2) FAC 107.

entities.text: Subhash Chand @ Subhash K. Aggarwal - Versus- State (Chandigarh Administration), Chandigarh, reported in 2011(2) FAC 107

The case of L. N.
Bangur & Others -Versus- The Food Inspector & Another, reported in (2011)2 FAC 340 of Kerala High Court and Gauhati High Court's decision in the case of Shri Dulal Mandal & Others -Versus- The State of Assam, reported in 2011(2) FAC 355 have also been referred.

sentences.text: Learned advocate appearing for the opposite party no. 1 countered by inviting the attention of this Court to the provisions of Section 17(1)(a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and argued that in view of the aforesaid provision the petitioner being the Director of the company cannot shirk his responsibility for the conduct of the business of the company.

In this context it would be profitable to refer to the relevant provisions of Section 17(1) of the Act which provides as follows :
Arnab Basu vs Bikash Chandra Chattopadhyay & Another on 18 December, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167329926/
1 "17. Offences by companies.

entities.text: Arnab Basu vs Bikash Chandra Chattopadhyay & Another on 18 December, 2017 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: - (1) Where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company - (a) (i) the person, if any, who has been nominated under sub-section (2) to be in charge of, and responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company (hereafter in this section referred to as the person responsible), or (ii) where no person has been so nominated,

every person who at the time the offence was committed was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company; and (b) the company, shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly:
Provided that nothing contained in this sub-section shall render any such person liable to any punishment provided in this Act if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge and that he exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence."
Curiously enough, there is no averment in the petition of complaint that the petitioner whose name figures therein as the accused no. 2 - Director of M/s.
Switz Food (P) Ltd. was in charge of and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business of the said company.

It appears that the complaint was filed by the Food Inspector, Bikash Chandra Chattopadhyay against (1) M/s.
Switz Food (P) Ltd., P-36 & 41, Kasba Industrial Estate, Kolkata-78, Ward -108, (2)
Arnab Basu - Director of M/s. Switz Food (P) Ltd., and (3) Indranil Ganguli- Seller and Person-in-Charge of M/s.
Switz Food (P) Ltd.

It is alleged in the petition of complaint that on November 19, 2001 the Food Inspector visited M/s. Switz Food (P) Ltd. for inspection and purchased an article of food namely Chicken Tandoori Roll after complying with the legal formalities.
A sample of the aforesaid food item was sent to the Public Analyst who opined that the said sample was adulterated.
It has further been alleged therein that the food item was sold to the Food Inspector by the accused no.3.

At this juncture it is significant to quote paragraph 8 of the petition of complaint which reads as follows :
"8. That on enquiry it is learnt that the said food belonged to the Accused No. 1 and that was stored/exposed in the shop for sale and Accused No. 3 was the person in-charge of the local affairs and was looking after the day to day business of Accused No. 1.
So both the seller, the Company/Firm/Proprietor and the person in charge of the business are liable for the offence under Section 16(1)a(i) read with Section 7 of the P.F.A. Act, 1954.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the circumstances the complainant prays that your honour may be pleased to issue summons against the accused person/persons abovenamed for offence committed u/S. 16(1)a(i) and 16(1)a (ii) of the P.F.A. Act, 1954 read with Section 7 and Rules 37A and 50 of the aforesaid Act and try the said accused and prays that your honour may be pleased to pass an order for the destruction of the seized/sealed stock of food at the cost of the accused party or pass an order for the forfeiture of the seized/sealed stock of food to the Calcutta Municipal Corporation, being the Local Authority or to pass such order or orders as your honour may deem fit and proper".

On perusal of the complaint it appears that there is not even a whisper therein that the accused no. 2 (petitioner herein) was in any way responsible for the affairs of the company or conduct of its business.
There is nothing in the complaint to indicate that the petitioner was the person in charge of the business and was managing the affairs of the company at the relevant point of time.
Evidently no case against the petitioner has been made out ex facie on the allegations in the complaint which discloses offence against the accused nos. 1 and 3 only.
In the circumstances, as no prima facie case has been made out against the petitioner, the proceeding against him is liable to be quashed.
Consequently, the application being C.R.R. 1438 of 2002 is allowed.
The criminal proceeding in Case No. 1D of 2002 as regards the petitioner named as the accused no. 2 in the petition of complaint is quashed.
The application is thus disposed of.
Interim order if any stands vacated.
The trial Court shall expedite the proceeding of Case No. 1D of 2002 and dispose of the same in accordance with law without granting unnecessary adjournment to either of the parties.
Urgent Photostat certified copy of this order, if applied for, shall be given to the parties upon compliance of requisite formalities.

( Asha Arora, J.)
